'''James:''' {{legend0|#7996e2|50–60%}} | title = U.S. senator | before_election = [[John Boozman]] | before_party = Republican Party (United States) | after_election = [[John Boozman]] | after_party = Republican Party (United States) | turnout = 50.81% {{decrease}} }} {{Elections in Arkansas sidebar}} The '''2022 United States Senate election in Arkansas''' was held on November 8, 2022, to elect a member to the [[United States Senate]] to represent the [[U.S. state|state]] of [[Arkansas]]. Incumbent [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]] Senator [[John Boozman]] ran for a third term.{{cite news |title=Senator Boozman seeks re-election in 2022 |url=https://www.swtimes.com/story/news/2021/03/15/senator-boozman-announces-re-election-bid-2022/4710195001/ |access-date=March 17, 2021 |agency=Southwest Times Record |date=March 15, 2021}} He won the May 24, 2022 Republican primary with 58.03% of the vote and the general election with 65.73% of the vote.{{Cite web |title=AP PROJECTS: Republican John Boozman wins reelection to U.S. Senate from Arkansas |url=https://www.ky3.com/2022/11/09/ap-projects-republican-john-boozman-wins-reelection-us-senate-arkansas/ |access-date=2022-11-09 |website=ky3 |date=November 9, 2022 |language=en}} This was the best performance for a Republican senator in the state's history, and was the first time for either U.S. Senate seat in Arkansas that Republicans won three consecutive elections. ==Republican primary== Incumbent senator [[John Boozman]] ran with the endorsement of former President [[Donald Trump]]. However, he attracted multiple opponents from the right who questioned his loyalty to Trump, attacking him for refusing to object to the results of the [[2020 United States presidential election]].{{cite web | url=https://arktimes.com/arkansas-blog/2022/04/05/boozman-blasted-for-private-remarks-about-trump | title=Boozman blasted for private remarks about Trump | date=April 5, 2022 }} Despite it being his first time running for office, former NFL football player [[Jake Bequette]] and his supporting groups raised over $2.6 million.{{cite web | url=https://swark.today/senate-candidate-jake-bequette-and-supporting-groups-raise-over-2-6-million-to-date/ | title=Senate Candidate Jake Bequette and Supporting Groups Raise over $2.6 Million to Date | access-date=April 19, 2022 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220415222242/https://swark.today/senate-candidate-jake-bequette-and-supporting-groups-raise-over-2-6-million-to-date/ | archive-date=April 15, 2022 | url-status=dead }} Boozman ultimately won with 58% of the vote, easily avoiding a runoff. ===Candidates=== ====Nominee==== * [[John Boozman]], incumbent U.S. senator ====Eliminated in primary==== * [[Jake Bequette]], former [[NFL]] player and U.S. Army veteran{{cite news |title=Former NFL player, Iraq war veteran Jake Bequette challenges Arkansas Sen. Boozman|url=https://www.foxnews.com/politics/former-nfl-player-iraq-war-veteran-bequette-challenges-arkansas-sen-boozman|access-date=July 12, 2021 |agency=Fox News|date=July 12, 2021}} *Heath Loftis, pastor{{cite news |title=Another challenger to John Boozman from the right |url=https://arktimes.com/arkansas-blog/2021/03/24/another-challenger-to-john-boozman-from-the-right |publisher=Arkansas Times |access-date=April 9, 2021 |date=March 24, 2021}} * Jan Morgan, [[gun range]] owner and candidate for [[governor of Arkansas]] in [[2018 Arkansas gubernatorial election|2018]]{{cite news |title=Former gubernatorial candidate Jan Morgan launches U.S. Senate bid |url=https://www.arkansasonline.com/news/2021/mar/17/former-gubernatorial-candidate-launches-bid-us-sen/ |access-date=March 18, 2021 |agency=Arkansas Democrat Gazette |date=March 17, 2021}} ====Withdrew==== * Michael Deel, corporate analyst{{Cite web|author=Staff Reports|title=Young Republican Michael Deel makes bid for U.S. Senate|url=https://www.swtimes.com/story/news/2021/05/10/republican-michael-deel-fort-smith-announces-run-u-s-senate/4921398001/|access-date=2021-05-10|website=Southwest Times Record|language=en-US}} ===Endorsements=== {{Endorsements box|title=John Boozman|list=;Executive branch officials *[[Sarah Huckabee Sanders]], former [[White House press secretary]] (2017–2019){{cite web|website=Northwest Arkansas Democrat Gazette|title=Gun-rights activist Jan Morgan kicks off Senate run|url=https://www.nwaonline.com/news/2021/mar/18/gun-rights-activist-kicks-senate-run/|author=Frank E.
